text:
Japan’s inflation-adjusted, PPP-comparable GDP per capita rose about twelvefold from 1950 to 2016, with standard Maddison Project series placing the gain at roughly 11–14 times (on the order of a 1,100–1,300 percent increase). In those reconstructions the level moved from a few thousand constant international dollars in 1950 to the mid-to-high $30,000s by 2016, and most of that rise came before the early-1990s slowdown.

CONFIDENCE: 68
